summary.neuroengineering: Recently admitted to the UC Davis M.S. in Biomedical Engineering (Fall 2026) and active neuroscience researcher working at the intersection of human intracranial electrophysiology, single-unit digital signal processing, and neurotechnology tooling. Experience includes spike sorting with Kilosort4, O-Sort, and SpikeInterface; building GPU-accelerated pipelines on AWS; and implementing Dark Horse Neuro / Neuralynx acquisition workflows for replay, compression-aware MED recording, and large-scale neural data handling. I look forward to a career in neural signal processing, neural acquisition systems, and BCI-related infrastructure.

Experienced with Python/SQL, SPSS, dashboards, and Microsoft 365 automation. Committed to equity-centered learning and improving health and housing outcomes.

bullets.text: Build a GPU-accelerated spike sorting pipeline for dense microelectrode arrays using Kilosort4 on AWS EC2 instances to support reproducible, high-throughput reprocessing of human intracranial recordings.

Sort single-unit activity from human Phase II epilepsy microwire recordings using MATLAB (O-Sort) and Python (SpikeInterface), with an emphasis on preserving unit-specific waveform structure for downstream analysis.
Curated a dataset of approximately 2 million hand-labeled waveforms for spike-vs-noise modeling and benchmarking.
Trained neural network models to classify putative single units versus noise, improving manual curation efficiency for human recordings.

projects.name: Dark Horse Neuro / Neuralynx acquisition pipeline
bullets: Built a Python orchestration layer to launch DHN-AQ headlessly over SSH, generate RC/CS session files, and coordinate Pegasus / NetCom replay workflows for human intracranial recordings.
Implemented an NRD replay bridge that re-broadcasts ATLAS-format UDP packets so archived Neuralynx sessions can be ingested by DHN-AQ as if hardware were live.
Automated compression-aware MED recording setup for 512-channel macro / micro configurations, including decimation, lossless/lossy options, and pre-flight network diagnostics.

projects.name: spike_discrim single-unit DSP workbench
bullets: Benchmarked low-latency waveform representations for real-time single-unit discrimination using curated OSort snippets, synthetic data, AUC, balanced accuracy, mutual information, and KNN purity.
Built a Numba-accelerated WeightBank population code to score spike-likeness and project waveforms into afferent activation space for clustering and unit-separation analysis.

projects.name: SNN Agent real-time spike sorting
bullets: Developed a streaming spiking neural network with bandpass filtering, Kalman noise gating, competitive STDP, and browser-based monitoring for live spike detection and sorting.
Evaluated 20 kHz real-time pipeline behavior across synthetic, .ncs, UDP, and LSL inputs with online decoding for closed-loop neurotech use cases.
